title: Cyberpunk 2077 Was Announced 8 Years Before You Could Play It
hook:
CD Projekt Red announced Cyberpunk 2077 in May 2012 and the first teaser promised it was coming when it's ready. Ready meant December 2020, after three delays in one year, and the game has now sold more than 40 million copies. Did you play it at launch, or wait for the fixes?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Cyberpunk 2077 was announced in two thousand twelve, more than eight years before anyone could play it? CD Projekt Red revealed the game at a press conference in Warsaw on May thirtieth of that year. The first teaser arrived in January two thousand thirteen and ended with a now famous promise: coming when it's ready. Ready took a long time. Then Keanu Reeves surprised the crowd at E3 in two thousand nineteen, revealing his role and announcing a release date for the following April. When a fan yelled that he was breathtaking, Keanu shouted it right back. Then the game was delayed three times in a single year, from April to September, to November, and finally December. When it finally launched that December, it sold thirteen million copies in the first ten days, even after refunds. After a rough start on the older consoles, Sony pulled the game from the PlayStation Store for six months. CD Projekt kept patching. By two thousand twenty three its Steam reviews had climbed to very positive, and the Phantom Liberty expansion followed. Today the game has passed forty million copies sold. And this week it arrived on Blizzard's Battle.net store, a few weeks after The Witcher 3 Remastered. Did you play it at launch, or wait for the fixes? Follow for more gaming history.
